tagline: Six steep, winding miles over to the Carmel River.
intro: Laureles Grade leaves Highway 68, about halfway between Salinas and Monterey, and heads for Carmel Valley. It is a steep, winding road of six miles, and at the far end it meets Carmel Valley Road.

The road shares its name with Rancho Los Laureles, a Mexican land grant along the Carmel River named for the California bay laurel. Juana Cota Boronda, whose family settled on the rancho in 1840, brought to Carmel Valley a white-yellow cheese made from a Spanish recipe. David Jack is credited with first marketing what came to be called Monterey Jack.

moments.title: Corral de Tierra
moments.text: Near the start of the grade lies the valley of Steinbeck's The Pastures of Heaven, where he and his sister Mary played below Castle Rock, the earthen fence behind the name.

moments.title: Garland Ranch Regional Park
moments.text: On Carmel Valley Road near the foot of the grade, the Rancho Loop Trail leads to a packing shed, a barn and a display of old farm equipment.
